solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Advocates for heathen princess facing saints over time

parts.note: being for something is being pro it
a heathen is a pagan
Di is the familiar name of Diana, Princess of Wales

indicators.note: the two saints sit over, that is either side of, the letter for time

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, so two saints are SS

explanation.surface: Campaigners speak up for a pagan princess who confronts saints across the ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' only places the princess next to the saints. 'over' wraps the two S's round T to give STS.
explanation.definitionFit: Propagandists are people who promote a cause, so they act as its advocates.

clue.text: The eminence of politicians in a part of London?

definitions.text: The eminence of politicians in a part of London?

parts.words: The eminence of politicians in a part of London?
parts.note: an eminence is a hill; a hill named after the house where politicians sit, which is a real open space in north London

explanation.walkthrough: 'eminence' sounds like a title for a great person, but here it means high ground. PARLIAMENT HILL is a rise on Hampstead Heath in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament Hill is a high point in London whose name joins the legislature with a hill, an eminence.

clue.text: Bob doesn't have top weight

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: to bob is to bounce up and down

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob is missing the heaviest weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name but is the verb to bounce. 'doesn't have top' drops its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a unit of weight in the imperial system, a sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: A male's been at sea — as have these chaps

definitions.text: A male's been at sea — as have these chaps

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A man has been out on the ocean, just as sailors have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges A MALES BEEN; the whole clue also describes the sailors, who have all been to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Able seamen are qualified naval ratings, sailors who by definition have been to sea.

clue.text: A non-drinker longing to make a case

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a non-drinker
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A teetotaller's yearning provides grounds for an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a case' suggests arguing; here 'case' is the briefcase.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché case is a slim briefcase, and the shortened name is used alone for it.

clue.text: Philosopher rushed up after theologian, hugging one

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the theologian piece
the theologian's letters wrap round the one, as if embracing it

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to rush is to tear along, past tense tore

explanation.surface: A thinker sprints upwards behind a cleric who is holding someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for rushed, as this is a down clue; 'hugging' has the theologian embrace the one. Diderot was a French Enlightenment philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was an eighteenth-century French philosopher and editor of the Encyclopédie.

clue.text: Playwright spotted outside front of Haymarket

indicators.note: the word for spotted goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: to spot something is to see it, past tense saw

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dramatist is seen in front of a West End theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Haymarket is a London street with a famous theatre, which makes a playwright fit the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright, author of Pygmalion.

clue.text: Informal ballot gets Labour politician c-cut up

parts.note: Jack Straw was a Labour Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the piece reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the stammer repeats the first letter of a word for cut, so lop becomes l-lop

explanation.surface: An unofficial vote leads a Labour MP to be stuttering and upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'c-cut' tells you to stutter the synonym too: LOP becomes LLOP, and 'up' turns it to POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an unofficial vote taken to gauge opinion, an informal ballot.

clue.text: Usually act in the manner that's appropriate for one of the top brass

definitions.text: act in the manner that's appropriate for one of the top brass
definitions.meaning: read literally, behave the way an army general would, giving orders and ruling

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: as a general, rule. 'Top brass' are senior military officers.
explanation.definitionFit: As a general rule is an idiom meaning in most cases, or usually.

clue.text: Dissolute gent, idler with curly hair

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, and here the letters are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A debauched, idle man has a head of curls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringleted describes hair arranged in ringlets, which are long curls.

clue.text: Large area from which a hilltop shortly becomes visible

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: the crest is the top of a hill

explanation.surface: A broad landscape from which the top of a hill soon comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but here trims the end of CREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres are units of land, and the plural is used loosely for a large expanse.

clue.text: Italian script containing English bits of news

indicators.note: the Italian and the script together hold the letter for English

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a script

explanation.surface: An Italian text has English news snippets inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual reports in a news bulletin or newspaper.

clue.text: Beef or fish?

definitions.meaning: to beef is to complain or grumble
a freshwater fish often kept in ponds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is the verb to complain, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain, a sense shared by slang beef, and a carp is a fish.

clue.text: First bit from some comedian? I may get carried away!

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a wag is a joker or comedian

explanation.surface: A comic's opening material hopes not to be swept off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the loot: thieves carry it away.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is stolen goods, which burglars carry off in a bag.

clue.text: Did one of the Spice Girls do nothing that might appeal to Aussie music lovers?

definitions.text: that might appeal to Aussie music lovers

parts.note: taken as written
Geri Halliwell, Ginger Spice in the 1990s British pop group
taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Did a Spice Girl do nothing that Australian music fans would like?
explanation.walkthrough: The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group; Geri is the one wanted. The didgeridoo is an Aboriginal Australian wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A didgeridoo is the traditional Australian drone instrument, so it appeals to Aussie music lovers.

clue.text: He meant to change to gas

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone intended to switch to gas heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a natural gas, the main component of the fuel piped to homes.

clue.text: Four-letter word that initially disturbed Margaret

indicators.note: the first letter of the word next to it
disturbed means upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude four-letter word upset a woman called Margaret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' suggests a swear word; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word made of four letters, from Greek tetra four.

clue.text: Not completely opulent, wearing ripped hat

indicators.note: the ripped word wears the other, holding it inside

parts.note: ripped means torn

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: opulent means rich

explanation.surface: Someone wealthy is wearing a tattered hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not completely' trims the last letter of the opulent word; 'wearing' puts what remains inside the ripped word, as a head wears a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Idiots trapped in cavern — utter stupidity

indicators.note: the answer is held within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Fools stuck in a cave show complete stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutters is British slang for crazy or foolish people, idiots.

clue.text: Earthquake's getting Melissa shaken up

indicators.note: the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A tremor shakes a woman called Melissa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earthquake's' works as an adjective: belonging to earthquakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismal means relating to earthquakes, as seismic does.

clue.text: Old woman good with pounds, top woman who wants a bargain?

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman
L is the symbol for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An old woman with money and a woman of rank seek a good deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top woman' is the Queen, ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggler argues over the price, someone who wants a better deal.

clue.text: I will be recognised as one in the chemistry group

definitions.text: I will be recognised as one in the chemistry group

parts.words: I will be recognised as one in the chemistry group
parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine, a member of group 17 of the periodic table

explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like a speaker but is iodine, the element with symbol I.
explanation.definitionFit: The halogens are the periodic-table group containing fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine.

clue.text: Leader possessed energy within

indicators.note: the energy letter goes inside the word for possessed

parts.note: possessed means had
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A leader was driven by energy from inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a person in charge, such as a head teacher or head of state.

clue.text: Philosopher's ism is rejected — bad!

indicators.note: the letters of the word is are thrown out of the word before them

parts.note: bad and ill both mean poor or harmful

explanation.surface: A thinker's doctrine is turned down as no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosopher's' reads as 'Philosopher is'. Take IS out of ISM to leave M, then add ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart Mill was a nineteenth-century English philosopher who wrote On Liberty.

clue.text: One animal or another found by English lake

parts.note: another animal, here a rat

explanation.surface: One creature or a second one is found next to a lake in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second animal, the rat.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, a fierce African animal.

clue.text: Gunlike device army's acquired with hesitation

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve, with 's
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: The military hesitantly acquires a new stun weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was the Territorial Army, the UK reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun weapon shaped like a pistol, firing darts that deliver a shock.

clue.text: Group of directors — all but one a beast

indicators.note: every letter except one, here the last

parts.note: a company's board is its group of directors

explanation.surface: Every board member but one is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig or uncastrated male pig, a beast.

clue.text: Good in exam about piece of music

indicators.note: the good letter goes inside the reversed exam
turned about, read backwards

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: Do well in an exam on a musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ORAL to LARO, with G inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a slow movement or piece, from the Italian tempo marking.

clue.text: Making fantastic dough's aim in the city

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Making a fortune is the goal in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' is a link; the s of 'dough's' counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mogadishu is a city, the capital of Somalia.

clue.text: Actress: 'From early morn on, I'm bouncing around'

indicators.note: the letters bounce about into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress claims she has been lively since dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was the American film actress of the 1950s.
